Pixel Blade · the mark · round seven

The
Vessel

A ring with real thickness, stood upright, cupping a world that was built rather than found — and the Monk sitting in it.

Round seven merges the two that worked: A's pine carried out on C's reach. Background texture removed, crop pulled in, contact shadow kept.

01 · The lead

A's tree,
C's reach

The merge is the whole round. A had the better pine — layered tiers of needle pad on a gnarled leaning trunk. C had the better argument — the subject growing out through the crescent's mouth and breaking the object's own silhouette, which is the one move struck said to borrow.

Ground texture is gone; it is flat tone now. The crop is tighter. The contact shadow stays, low and directional off the house light.

02 · Night

The scoop
turns bronze

Confirmed again on the new crop. Night is not the day plate dimmed — the concave inner face reads pale grey on paper and bronze on sumi, which is what tokens.css requires, since bronze measures 2.05:1 on paper and hands its role to oxide. Roles held, values swapped.

EN1 is filed as an accident worth keeping: the crescent closed into a full ring, which is not this concept at all — it is the Rim Window, the annulus that carries the world in its rim. A different idea, arrived at sideways.

EN2 · bronze scoop · 83.6% dark · the night lead
EN1 · closed to a ring · not this concept — filed
03 · Held, not discarded

Round six
stays on the table

Kept per your call. A and C are now parents rather than candidates. B and D are still live in their own right — D especially, which introduced the mirror floor from dreamed garden without being asked to.

04 · The die

Geometry,
struck in code

Underneath the renders, vessel.py holds the geometry: two discs, one subtracted, given a real cross-section — a rounded shoulder with a concave scoop cut near the inner edge — lit at 214°, z 0.34. No outline exists anywhere in the file. Every edge is a place where two values meet.

vessel.py --day
vessel.py --night

One thing the tighter crop exposed: before feathering, E3 sat at 38.9% ground and failed. The feather is what recovers it — the falloff to page ground adds the very margin the crop removed. Crop and ground floor are the same dial, and the vignette is what lets you have both.

Hue across all six sits at 15–30 — the lit-world family running into bronze at 29. Nothing strays.

06 · Small

Handed to
the kamon

The object still stops carrying its world below roughly 128px. That is no longer a problem to solve here — a kamon takes the favicon and anywhere else genuinely small.

Worth noting what that decision buys: the kamon is a flat mark, and it works at 16px precisely because it is not pretending to be an object. The vessel and the kamon are the two halves the system has been missing — forge and livery, made and said.

07 · Open

Three decisions

E2 or E1

E2 is the stronger argument — the reach clears the object and the canopy has real structure. E1 is warmer, quieter, and the scoop reads better. Both pass. E3 has the best reach and the worst ground.

E4 should be struck

Mirroring puts the lit inner face on the side turned away from the house light. Two sources is a bug, and this is that bug arrived at by flipping rather than by lighting. Worth a look before it goes, in case the flip is worth re-lighting properly.

The kasa still needs a ruling

monk.md gives him no hat. If it stays, that file needs a line permitting it at mark scale, or the next session reads a contradiction and quietly removes it.
